chen2026fabscore: Automated AI research can accelerate discovery, but AI-generated papers may fabricate results. FabScore evaluates such papers by extracting numerical results and figure labels as individual claims, then having a coding agent check each claim through static analysis and code execution, assigning one of six verdicts such as fabricated, reproducible, or unverifiable. Human evaluation gives it 98.6 percent precision in detecting fabrications. Applied to 144 papers, it finds a 21.2 percent claim-level fabrication rate, with over 70 percent of AI-authored conference submissions containing fabrications and experiment fabrication the most common type, while current AI reviewers miss more than 85 percent of detected cases.
fu2026adamrec: Multimodal recommenders usually fuse visual and textual signals statically, even though some queries need fine-grained visual cues and others are better served by text, so indiscriminate fusion hurts quality. AdaM-Rec is an LLM-based framework that routes between modalities dynamically per query. From structured natural-language item and preference representations, it generates pseudo-queries matching the actual query granularity but pointing to the user's positively interacted items, then uses proxy recall to estimate which modality is more reliable in analogous situations and optimizes routing agentically. It performs routed recall, enriches candidates with collaborative items, and ranks by query and preference relevance, outperforming state-of-the-art multimodal recommenders.
fu2026contextnav: Multimodal in-context learning adapts models from a few examples, but hand-picked contexts are laborious while retrieved contexts bring noisy, structurally inconsistent samples. ContextNav is an agentic framework that combines scalable automated retrieval with human-like curation. It builds a resource-aware multimodal embedding pipeline over a vector database, uses agentic retrieval and structural alignment to assemble noise-robust contexts, and plans its workflow through an Operational Grammar Graph that adapts to downstream feedback. The closed loop refines context selection from ICL performance itself, reaching state-of-the-art results across diverse vision-language datasets.
fu2026videostir: Long-video question answering is limited by context windows, and existing retrieval-augmented methods flatten videos into independent segments and match semantics explicitly, missing structure and intent-implicit cues. VideoStir structures a video as a clip-level spatio-temporal graph and performs multi-hop retrieval to connect distant but related events. An MLLM-backed intent scorer ranks frames by alignment with the query's reasoning purpose, and a curated 600K-frame dataset, IR-600K, trains this alignment. Without auxiliary information, the framework matches state-of-the-art long-video baselines, shifting long-video RAG from flat semantic matching toward structured, intent-aware reasoning.
ge2025acl: How a graph is described to a language model can change its reasoning, but this ordering effect has been overlooked. The paper presents the first comprehensive study of how graph descriptive order affects LLM performance, evaluating four description orders across six graph problems with six mainstream models. Ordered descriptions significantly improve structural comprehension, robustness to ordering varies by task, and the impact closely tracks inherent task characteristics. The findings show that prompt ordering is a controllable factor for graph reasoning and open a route to improving performance through strategic graph description design.
ge2025mrfd: Large vision-language models hallucinate because they cannot verify information across different image regions. Multi-Region Fusion Decoding is a training-free method that models inter-region consistency: it finds salient regions with cross-attention, generates an initial response for each region under chain-of-thought-style prompts, and weighs the responses by Jensen-Shannon divergence so that consistent, reliable views dominate. A consistency-aware fusion then combines per-region predictions into the final answer. Across multiple LVLMs and hallucination benchmarks, the decoding method reduces hallucinations and improves factual grounding without any model update.
ge2026focusing: Vision-language models degrade in complex visual scenes, and existing fixes require extra training or external segmentation. Analyzing attention, the work finds that visual complexity correlates with attention entropy and harms reasoning, that attention refines from global scanning in shallow layers to focused convergence in deeper ones, and that contrasting attention maps from general versus task-specific queries separates signal from visual noise. Building on this, CARVE is a training-free method that extracts task-relevant visual signals by contrasting attention maps at the pixel level. On seven benchmarks it improves visual perception on both recent and older models.
ge2026prism: Prompt highlighting steers a model toward user-specified text spans, but existing key-editing methods extract directions that mix relevant and shared context structure. Prism-delta decomposes the difference between positive and negative cross-covariance matrices to maximize discriminative energy while discarding shared directions, gives each attention head a continuous softplus importance weight, and extends the steering to value representations. Across four benchmarks and five models it matches or beats the best prior method on 19 of 20 configurations by up to 13 percent while halving the fluency cost, and improves long-context retrieval by up to 5.1 percent with negligible memory overhead under FlashAttention.
ge2026skillforge: Memory-augmented reinforcement learning lets LLM agents reuse skills, but retaining every skill indiscriminately lets obsolete or harmful entries accumulate and mislead the agent. SkillForge manages a skill library through a fitness-driven lifecycle of trial, active, stable, and retired states that co-evolves skills with the policy. A pre-RL phase uses the base model's own rollouts to retire low-fitness skills before supervised fine-tuning, then reinforcement learning continues selective retirement, stabilization, and LLM-guided mutation. Across interactive agent benchmarks it reaches the highest aggregate success rate, up to 7.8 percent over the strongest baseline, with a compact skill library, and it releases a 5K-record dataset of filtered trajectories and retirement events.
ge2026streaming: Streaming video models must answer queries at any moment under fixed memory budgets, and indiscriminate history injection can dilute current-scene perception. The work frames this as budgeted online latent evidence allocation and proposes SelectStream, which keeps the current observation directly visible to a frozen VLM while exposing history only through a compact query-conditioned evidence budget. Surprise-driven adaptive windowing decides when to write, priority-preserving consolidation decides what to keep, and a fixed-capacity latent memory graph supports query-conditioned retrieval. Retrieved evidence is injected as latent tokens without replaying frames. On StreamingBench it reaches 82.67 percent, on OVO-Bench 67.03 percent, while preserving 74.4 percent average accuracy on offline video benchmarks.
han2026dynamic: Diffusion language models support bidirectional attention and parallel generation, suiting format-constrained outputs such as JSON or reasoning templates, but fixed anchor positions rigidly enforce spans and cause truncated reasoning or redundant text. Dynamic Infilling Anchors is a training-free method that estimates end-anchor positions on the fly to adjust generation length before iterative infilling, keeping structure correct and content coherent. On reasoning benchmarks it substantially improves format compliance and answer accuracy, with significant zero-shot gains on GSM8K and MATH, offering a robust path to reliable structure-aware generation.
hao2025making: Jailbreak attacks red-team vision-language models, but not every adversarial optimization step helps, and accepting all steps can lower attack success. HKVE, Hierarchical Key-Value Equalization, selectively accepts gradient updates based on the distribution of attention scores across layers so that every step moves the attack forward. It achieves attack success rates of 75.08 percent on MiniGPT-4, 85.84 percent on LLaVA, and 81.00 percent on Qwen-VL, outperforming prior methods by 20.43, 21.01, and 26.43 points, while needing fewer iterations and less compute. The result highlights how layer-wise attention statistics can guide more efficient adversarial optimization.
